title: Mentoring the Machine — Eric Hou, Augment Code
talk_summary: Eric Hou of Augment Code describes treating AI agents as perpetually junior engineers that must be mentored with context, constraints, and outcomes rather than assigned tickets, and argues the real bottleneck is organizational knowledge infrastructure. He shows a demo where one engineer parallelizes a design component, a staging incident, and a gRPC remediation across multiple agents in half a day.

takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of specifying implementation steps, the engineer gives the agent the desired outcome, relevant context, and boundary constraints, then lets it explore the codebase and produce an RFC or change.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I'm giving AI the outcomes, the context, constraints, and I'd have it perform the same tasks I'd expect of any other engineer.

takeaways.what_they_do: When colleagues asked how to get the same agent behavior, the engineer shared his 'memories' file so learned patterns and task lists propagate across the team.

takeaways.technique: Parallel workstreams with human on critical path
takeaways.what_they_do: The engineer hands off independent tasks (design component, log parsing/git bisect, comms) to separate agents running in background while personally focusing on the hardest part of the incident.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I'm orchestrating parallel AI work streams while I get to focus on the critical path of solving the on call issue.
takeaways.numbers: gRPC upgrade touched 12 services, 20,000 lines of code; normally ~3 weeks of engineering work

takeaways.what_they_do: Because knowledge infrastructure makes prototyping cheap, teams build multiple divergent prototypes simultaneously and converge on the best using real metrics instead of debating designs in meetings.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Instead of guessing at what might be the best approach, we can rapidly prototype, iterate, test, and then converge on a real decision based on real metrics

takeaways.what_they_do: They connect codebase, docs, Linear, and meeting-intelligence tools (e.g., Granola) via MCP/native integrations so agents and a Slackbot can answer context questions and emit tasks automatically.
takeaways.evidence_quote: begin integrating data sources using things like MCP and augment native integrations to create the beginnings of your knowledge infrastructure

takeaways.what_they_do: After finding the bad commit and reverting, agents drafted the postmortem doc and began exploring remediation, giving humans an evaluation artifact rather than raw diffs.
takeaways.evidence_quote: They've started writing up a postmortem doc and already started exploring remediation.
